title: fix(gateway): wait for lifecycle ownership during restart
body:
Fixes #146142

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**Maintainer edits:** This branch is in `openclaw/openclaw`; maintainers with repository write access can update it directly.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users restarting a supervised Gateway could get an immediate startup failure while another OpenClaw process still held lifecycle ownership. Repeated failed starts could exhaust systemd's start limit and leave the Gateway down.

Reported by @waynegault (#146142).

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway acquisition now waits for lifecycle-coordinator contention under a five-minute monotonic deadline, with backoff from 250 ms to 2 seconds. It logs the initial wait and successful acquisition, and includes the elapsed wait in a terminal ownership error. The deadline loop is shared with the startup-migration lease fix from #120959; migration owner classification and polling cadence stay intact.

Supervised startup recognizes lifecycle contention and passes the same absolute deadline into acquisition, including time spent loading startup code. A healthy port cannot turn coordinator contention into successful startup. Generated systemd units allow ten starts per 300 seconds while retaining the five-second restart delay; both documented unit examples match. Launchd already has throttling without a finite start-limit latch.

The coordinator remains an anonymous SQLite lock. Holder identity is a follow-up pending Peter's persistence design decision. A foreign live owner receives the same bounded wait and still fails if it never releases; the code never steals ownership. Normal restart already releases ownership before handing off in both v2026.9.3 and this branch, so the reporter's exact overlapping process remains unidentified.

## User Impact

A restarted Gateway waits, with a generous bounded budget, for its predecessor to release lifecycle ownership instead of failing immediately and tripping systemd's start limit.

The candidate Gateway owns this behavior, so an older installed updater or existing unit can benefit without learning a new handoff marker. The revised systemd limits apply when the service definition is rewritten. No configuration options, dependencies, schemas, or retained-state semantics change.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the new real cross-process coordinator tests failed immediately on a predecessor scheduled to release after two seconds, and the permanent-owner test received the old error without a wait. The supervised-classification test independently failed on lifecycle contention.
- The existing systemd unit test failed before the template change: expected burst 10, received 5.
- Focused proof: **314 tests passed**, covering lifecycle and role locks, migration leases, supervised startup, run-loop shutdown, restart sentinels, systemd units, and launchd plists.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed, including production/test typechecks, lint, schema guards, and zero runtime import cycles. `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent autoreview: **scoped-clean through P2**.
- Linux Testbox: **remote `pnpm build` and real systemd restart passed**, with candidate source hashes verified. Node 24.19.0 / systemd 255.4. An independent synthetic holder retained the actual coordinator until two seconds after the replacement logged waiting. Readiness succeeded; PID changed; `NRestarts=0`, `Result=success`, `ExecMainStatus=0`, and no failed-start message. The owned service and Testbox were cleaned up.

```text
waiting for gateway-lifecycle ownership held by another OpenClaw process, up to 300 s
gateway-lifecycle ownership acquired after 3.8 s
ActiveState=active  SubState=running  NRestarts=0  Result=success
```

[Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34704311503), lease `tbx_01m2b60qf71cpz0zhr9p7z153q`, wrapper exit 0. Provider cleanup can mark the hosting Actions run cancelled; the proof command itself passed.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/infra/gateway-lock.test.ts \
  src/infra/gateway-lock.roles.test.ts \
  src/infra/state-database-coordinator.test.ts \
  src/infra/startup-migration-checkpoint.test.ts \
  src/cli/gateway-cli/run.supervised-lock.test.ts \
  src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-restart-sentinel.test.ts \
  src/daemon/systemd-unit.test.ts \
  src/daemon/launchd-plist.test.ts
```

Production grows by 93 lines for bounded asynchronous acquisition, diagnostics, and deadline propagation; the migration polling loop is shared rather than duplicated. There is no persistent ownership representation change.

CI also exposed an obsolete whole-module lock mock in CLI option coverage. Removing that mock restored the real timeout, contention classifier, and error class; all **94 CLI option/lifecycle tests passed** (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/gateway-cli/run.option-collisions.test.ts`). No assertions were weakened.

The first CI run exposed the infra test-root cap (701 roots versus the existing 700 limit). Both new ownership regressions were consolidated into the existing Gateway lock-role test file, preserving the cap and all assertions. The consolidated Gateway lock-role suite and repository partition/cap suite then passed **29 tests**:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/gateway-lock.roles.test.ts test/scripts/tsgo-core-test-shards.test.ts
```

**Published restart driver × candidate:** Exact npm `openclaw@2026.9.3` ran `gateway restart --preserve-definition --json` against the candidate under the same injected contention. It exited 0 with `result=restarted`, preserved the unit bytes, and produced a ready successor after a 3.8-second ownership wait with `NRestarts=0`. Runtime source hashes remained unchanged through the test-only consolidation. [Published-driver Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34704909786), lease `tbx_01m2b6pjepvdw2wj60sgv8hnf9`, wrapper exit 0; service, profile, and lease cleaned up. Setup initially hit the released CLI's canonical-path and enabled-unit guards; the final fixture used its supported named-profile layout and normal service enablement.

These Linux cells inject contention; they do not establish the original production holder or WSL2-specific behavior. The compatibility cell covers the published restart driver, not a full npm update.


Two unrelated failures were identified in the merged CI revision for head `cafce22616e` (main `d8312aab8aca`):

- `checks-node-compact-small-29`: `gateway-other` has 701 roots on that main revision versus 700 on this branch. Main PR #145602 / `31c8b990cb5c` added the worker-metrics test; this branch changes no Gateway test roots or shard configuration. This is separate from the corrected infra-root increase above.
- `checks-windows-node-test-2`: `update-managed-service-handoff-database-publication.test.ts` expects “changed during initialization” but receives “file is not a database” on Node 24.21.0. The test and its 265-file static dependency closure, package/lock files, and relevant runner inputs are unchanged by this branch; none of the changed lifecycle acquisition modules is in that closure. The exact Windows cause remains for its owner to investigate.

Both existing guards/assertions are retained. **Final-head CI passed** for `5c6dcc64d0005c6bac5df1d08f4b398b0baf44b4`: [completed successful run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34707617514). The earlier failures above are historical; the current check rollup is green.

## ClawSweeper review

The latest completed review of `5c6dcc64d0005c6bac5df1d08f4b398b0baf44b4` found no code or security defects. No code fixups were needed. **Skipped: identify the original WSL2 holder and prove a full npm update before merge.** The maintainer explicitly approved landing the bounded lifecycle-contention repair with these documented limitations: real Linux cross-process contention and the published 2026.9.3 restart driver prove the changed boundary. Identifying the original holder and adding coordinator holder identity remain follow-ups, with the latter pending a persistence decision.
